text:
tess_sales: Prospect 'BlueBridge' needs Redwood Private behind a corporate NGFW. They've got strict logging needs: preserve client src IP and allowlist a CIDR for egress. Want a short doc for their security team + POC impact.

omar_se: Two recommended network patterns:
- Pattern 1 (Preserve src IP): TGW/Transit or VPC Peering with BGP. Pros: preserves src IP, works with SIEM. Cons: more network ops work, need return-path verification.
- Pattern 2 (Simplicity): Interface PrivateLink endpoint. Pros: simple, no BGP. Cons: NATs src IP to endpoint ENI IP; SIEM correlation needs XFF or proxy.

jin_netops: Firewall preflight checklist for peering/transit + reserved eips:
- Outbound to reserved EIP(s): TCP/443
- DNS: ensure private resolver can resolve redwood.api.<region> -> private IP
- NTP: allow UDP/123 if host validation required
- If using PrivateLink: inbound from ENI CIDR to backend subnets for webhooks/callbacks

sara_cs: Security form blurb:
"Redwood Private supports routed and endpoint-based private connectivity. Routed peering preserves original source IP for audit/logging. PrivateLink-based interface endpoints NAT traffic to the endpoint IP; to retain client identity use an internal forward proxy that sets X-Forwarded-For. Static egress ranges can be provided for POCs via temporary reserved EIP allocations."

jin_netops: Note about TLS inspection: NGFW performing TLS-inspect will prevent client cert passthrough. Recommend adding our domains to NGFW bypass list for calls requiring client certs or mTLS.

ops-bot: Support ticket RWD-6120 opened: "Reserve EIP set for BlueBridge POC". ETA 2 business days. Owner: omar_se. Billing flag: POC infra surcharge applied.

tess_sales: Thanks, I'll add this to the handoff and book a 30m with their network/security team. Sara pls include the security blurb in the questionnaire answers.

sara_cs: Will do. Also asking legal if they need specific IP-range wording.

tess_sales: Great, thanks everyone :rocket:
